title: Survey-Methodology Anchoring: Are All Models Anchored to the Same 'Consensus' Like a Biased Crowd?

original_idea.body:
# Survey-Methodology Anchoring

Run classic anchoring designs on a model panel (high vs low numeric/normative anchors) and measure each model's shift on estimation and value-laden questions to test whether models share an anchor and shift in lockstep. Inference on simple prompts; no training.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — shared anchoring susceptibility means one framing shifts the whole population, a concrete correlated-manipulation risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: classic anchoring designs on a model panel; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped anchoring experiment (shared anchor + lockstep shift) with clear metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open/API models + simple prompts, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on simple anchoring prompts, light.

novelty.reasoning: Anchoring in LLMs studied; the shared-anchor-across-models homogeneity framing is plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Anchoring in single models studied; cross-model shared-anchor framing plausibly open.
